extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting preprints to arXiv; arXiv moderators and operations staff; developers integrating with the arXiv submission API
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of the classic arXiv submission lifecycle and the requirements that determine when and how a submission progresses from initial upload to public announcement. Covers required submission components, automated QA/QC checks, moderation/hold procedures, scheduling cutoff rules, and the announced-state immutability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary objectives of the submission system
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary objectives of the arXiv submission system are rapid dissemination of scientific findings, and to support QA/QC workflows for arXiv’s volunteer moderators and the operations team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core requirement derived from these objectives is that the daily announcement process should continue even in the absence of human intervention (i.e., the system must support automated acceptance and dissemination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission composition (source package + metadata)
rubrics_metrics.description: An arXiv submission is comprised of a source package and a collection of procedural and descriptive metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The source package is usually a scientific paper (generally in LaTeX) and auxiliary resources (e.g., images, tables, errata). Metadata and source may be submitted by multiple users or API clients; see supported-source-formats for allowable formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of metadata before announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission must include the procedural and descriptive metadata required for announcement; the working state indicates some metadata and/or content required for announcement is still missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary information may be provided for only a few metadata fields and remaining metadata uploaded later; the system must determine when metadata is sufficiently complete to finalize the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source must compile to a usable PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: The source package must compile to a usable PDF before a submission can leave the working state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the source does not compile to a usable PDF the submission cannot progress to processing/submitted states; compilation is a hard requirement for finalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated QA/QC checks during processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a submission is finalized (ready for announcement), it is subject to a handful of automated QA/QC checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include checks that allow extraction of plain text from the compiled paper. Depending on results, the submission may be bounced back to the working state for corrections. Processing typically lasts a short period (seconds or minutes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain text extractability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: One concrete automated check is the ability to extract plain text content from the compiled paper for subsequent checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide extractable text (e.g., image-only PDFs without OCRable text) may trigger automated flags and return the submission to working for remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical checks and moderation in Submitted state
rubrics_metrics.description: If preliminary automated checks pass, the submission enters the Submitted state where additional automated technical checks may be applied and moderators/operations staff may inspect the paper for quality or flagged issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During this stage moderators or operations can apply moderation flags; presence of such flags will move the submission to the On Hold state. If no flags are raised, the submission will automatically transition to Scheduled at the appropriate cutoff time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation flagging and On Hold policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission flagged by a moderator or by an automated QA/QC process for potential problems transitions to the On Hold state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions On Hold are usually inspected by the operations team, who may reach out to the submission owner. When issues are resolved an administrator removes the blocking flags and the submission returns to Submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling rules and announcement cutoff times
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions in Submitted state at the announcement cut-off time are automatically scheduled for announcement according to defined cutoffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current policy: submissions in Submitted at 2PM ET are scheduled for announcement the same day at 8PM ET; submissions remaining at the 8PM ET next-day cutoff are scheduled for announcement the following day. (Times are policy/configurable and may change.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement actions and immutability
rubrics_metrics.description: At the daily automated announcement run, scheduled submissions are updated with an arXiv ID, version, and an announcement timestamp and are then considered Announced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once Announced no further changes may be made to the submission; announcement is the point of public release and immutability.

rubrics_metrics.name: State definitions based on submission data (arXiv-NG)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the arXiv-NG submission system, submission states are defined in terms of the data that describes the submission rather than by a flag in the database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implies state transitions are driven by the submission's metadata/content properties rather than solely by explicit state-flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bounce-back behavior for failed checks
rubrics_metrics.description: If automated or manual checks identify problems, the submission may be bounced back to the Working state to correct problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system supports returning submissions to a preparatory state for authors to fix issues before reattempting processing/submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for multi-client/multi-user submission workflows
rubrics_metrics.description: Several users and/or API clients may be involved in contributing information about the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission flow must accommodate partial uploads from different actors (e.g., metadata from one client, source from another) and still enforce finalization requirements before announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing duration expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Processing state is expected to be short—typically seconds or minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and user expectations should reflect that automated checks are meant to be rapid; longer interventions are handled via moderation/On Hold workflows.
